Case study · Kathleen Savio, Illinois

An “accident” that wasn't

Accident
2004 · What it looked like

Found in a dry bathtub. Ruled an accidental drowning.

→
Homicide
2007–08 · New autopsy

Body exhumed. Bruises and a head wound didn't fit a fall.

→
Guilty
2012 · What changed

Ex-husband convicted of murder. 38 years.

Takeaways

Three things to remember

1Facts, not guiltThe court decides guilt

So, can a body testify in court?

8
Quick quiz · did it stick?

Five questions

1Who is often elected and doesn't have to be a doctor?

Medical examiners are appointed doctors.

2Which one is a manner of death?

Gunshot wound = cause. Blood loss = mechanism.

3Heart attack, then the crash. Manner?

The heart attack came first.

4Can an autopsy give the exact minute of death?

Temperature, stiffness, and blood pooling all vary.

5What tracks every person who handled a piece of evidence?

It proves evidence wasn't swapped or tampered with.
